_about: SPEC-106's ranking regression battery: expected top-3 recall results per
Conditions are fixed by that test and must not change without a new
battery: embeddings OFF (so retrieval is deterministic FTS-only, which is
what CI runs), access counters NOT recorded (so one query cannot influence
the next), and the clock frozen at 2026-08-23T12:00:00Z (decay reads one).
`top` is an ordered prefix: the first min(3, len(top)) results must be
exactly these permalinks, in this order. `why` records the judgment the
row encodes, so a future weight change shows up as an argument about a
stated intent rather than as a diff of opaque permalinks.
Golden-vault caveat worth knowing when reading these rows: only the
inbox/ captures carry a `created` date, so every other note scores the
neutral `unknown_recency`. Engine-written notes always carry timestamps
(the write path stamps created/modified), so a real vault exercises the
recency term far more than this fixture can.

commit messages.why: The rule that answers it is the only match; nothing to reorder.

files are truth.why: The decision named by the query wins even though Vault Engine is the more central note — decay must not demote an on-the-nose match.

api gateway.why: Title match first; the second gateway project and the decision behind it follow.

who owns the recall engine.why: An ownership question is answered by the person, not the project — she is the only note whose observation says 'Recall engine lead'.

vault doctor.why: The runbook is the answer; the two notes that reference the doctor follow.

MIT license.why: A deliberate close call: the fresh capture keeps the top slot it earned from retrieval, and the ADR sits right behind it. If a weight change swaps these two, that is a defensible outcome — re-record the row and say so.

rate limit.why: Recent capture first, then the note holding the actual value, then the note that embeds it.

pricing.why: Direct match ahead of the note that embeds it one level further out.

release process.why: Single match; guards against a filter accidentally excluding processes.

response length.why: The per-model variant note: recall must return it whole for every caller, with one variant served.

importer.why: The importer project ahead of the migration that depends on it.

curator retries.why: An inbox capture is recallable — the inbox is staging, not a hiding place.

onboarding a new client.why: A multi-word natural-language query still lands on the process note.
